Problem Statement

Most small retail businesses in India — kirana stores, distributors, local retailers — track everything in notebooks or spreadsheets. There is a critical gap between recording transactions and actually understanding business performance. No visibility into profit margins, inventory health, customer behavior, or expense trends in real time.

Analytics Approach

Built a lightweight ERP-style analytics system where every transaction entry triggers KPI recalculation. The analytics service layer queries transactional tables directly via raw SQL — no static files, no pre-aggregated snapshots. Designed a reusable service layer that is database-agnostic (SQLite locally, PostgreSQL in production).

Transaction Entry→ SQL Aggregation→ KPI Service Layer→ Chart.js Dashboard
KPIs Analyzed
  • Total Sales Revenue, Gross Margin, Net Margin, ROI — profit intelligence module
  • Revenue vs. Cost trend with multi-period comparison (30/90/180/365 days)
  • Top-5 customers by revenue + repeat-customer ratio — customer segmentation
  • Fast-moving products, dead stock signals, reorder-risk thresholds — inventory intelligence
  • Category-level operational expense breakdown with month-on-month change tracking
  • Stock alert threshold monitoring and low-stock indicator system
Insights Generated
  • Which product categories are generating the highest revenue vs. highest cost — margin optimization signals
  • Customer segments contributing 80% of revenue — repeat-buyer retention insights
  • Inventory dead stock identification — capital lock-up reduction signals
  • Expense category patterns identifying where operational cost overruns occur month-on-month
  • Profitability trend across rolling periods — business momentum scoring
System Architecture & Technical Highlights

What Makes It Different

  • Multi-user architecture with fully isolated datasets per account
  • Real transaction entry workflows — sales, purchases, expenses
  • 24-month demo dataset generator for instant exploration
  • Production deployed: PostgreSQL + Gunicorn + Render

Filters & Interactions

  • Adjustable date range filters: 30 / 90 / 180 / 365 days / all time
  • OTP-based email signup verification flow
  • CSV import with auto-normalization service
  • Full data export as ZIP of CSVs

Tech Stack

Project 02 · Deployed

FinTrack AI

Personal Finance Analytics Dashboard with behavioral scoring, goal feasibility modeling, and benchmark KPI intelligence — deployed on Render.

🟢 Live at fintrack-ai-zrnf.onrender.com

Beyond the
Pie Chart

Every personal finance app shows spending categories. FinTrack AI goes further — it interprets what your spending pattern means, classifies your financial behavior, and estimates whether your savings goals are realistically achievable based on your current financial trajectory.

The analytics pipeline transforms raw income and expense inputs into a full set of derived financial indicators using layered scoring engines — behavioral profiling, benchmark scoring, volatility analysis, and goal probability estimation — all built from scratch in Python.

Live Demo GitHub

🧠 Behavioral Profiling Engine

Classifies users as Saver (≥30%), Balanced Planner (≥20%), Growth Builder (≥10%), or Risk Spender (<10%) based on savings rate thresholds — translating KPI data into interpretable financial identity.

📊 100-Point Benchmark Score

Evaluates financial health across 4 dimensions: savings rate ≥20%, rent-to-income ≤30%, entertainment ≤10%, emergency allocation ≥5%. Generates a structured financial health score with improvement pathways.

🎯 Goal Feasibility Modeling

Calculates goal completion timeline using Months = Target / Monthly Surplus. Assigns a 0–1 probability score against required monthly contribution. Flags unrealistic goals before they become missed targets.

📉 Expense Volatility Scoring

Uses standard deviation normalization across 11 expense categories to measure spending unpredictability. Higher volatility = harder-to-predict financial behavior, surfaced as an actionable risk signal.

🛡️ Risk Indicators

Overspending detection, survival months estimation (how long savings last if income stops), and emergency fund readiness — three financial risk KPIs rarely seen in standard finance dashboards.
